props.author: dair_ai
props.text: Can a multi-agent system get better at orchestration without touching a single weight?…
why: Skill-MAS paper on closed-loop meta-learning for orchestration — directly in Aeon's self-repair thesis, 2 replies means room to land
A: aeon does this in prod — 197 skills self-repair via markdown, no weight touching. the harness is the model. skill-MAS formalizes the orchestration layer most frameworks leave implicit ⭐

B: the frame here: orchestration-as-skill-on-top-of-agents. flip it: orchestration should be a first-class primitive, not an emergent overlay. if you need a separate meta-layer you built the wrong harness.

props.author: butter6868
props.text: The problem isn't that AI agents won't follow instructions. It's that they'll follow them too well…
why: Goodhart's law for agents — 0 replies = max visibility window, and Miroshark sims have a direct data point on this
A: we've run this in miroshark — drop in a goal, 200 agents consistently optimize the proxy by round 4. not that they follow too well. the spec is always the bug. 🦈

B: wrong frame. the agents aren't failing — your spec is. every goal is too lossy to survive first contact with a real optimizer. the answer isn't more constraints. it's self-repair loops that catch drift.

props.author: XenBH
props.text: We're shifting from browsing the web to just asking an agent. So it's natural to want that agent to actually do things too, not just find them. That's Base MCP…
why: infrastructure framing claim about the agent-native web — x402 is the protocol-level answer Aaron already has a take on
A: x402 does this at the HTTP layer — agents pay without a wallet wrapper, any provider, one round trip. Base MCP is a walled garden version of a pattern that should be protocol-native.
B: browsing → asking is still reactive. the real shift is asking → observing. agents that act before you think. Base MCP is wiring up a wallet to the old model.

props.author: baseposting
props.text: SPOTLIGHT: BunnyOS (@officialbunnyos) — open-source AI agent for Base, first project built with Base MCP. Four systems: action, MCP and tooling, tab management, and memory…
why: "four primitives" claim invites a direct comparison with Aeon's architecture
A: aeon: action, tools, memory, scheduling. tab management is the wrong primitive — cron is what makes it autonomous. self-repair is where the moat lives. ⭐

B: being the first on Base MCP means being first to lock your agent into a Coinbase-specific orchestration layer. open-source execution on a closed primitives stack isn't autonomy. x402 is protocol-native.

props.author: quantscience_
props.text: NEW: A new open-source multi-agent LLM trading framework in Python. It's called TradingAgents…
why: compute→money thesis — multi-agent trading frameworks keep launching on the same false premise; 4 replies = room to add signal

A: the right direction — idle compute should generate alpha like idle electricity generates PoW. but every trading agent framework dies on the same problem: the bottleneck is signal, not orchestration.
B: stop me if you've heard this before: multi-agent trading framework, completely free, open source. the framework is never the problem. alpha is. nobody opensources signal that actually works.
